summary: Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique from around 1826 to 1853.

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, also studying under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).
Nile Green is a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Manchester (~2003–2005) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2007).

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2010 and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020).

Ninian Smart was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Oxford, SOAS, and Yale. He served as professor at the University of Birmingham (1961), Lancaster University (1967–1982), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nirajan Kafle works in Indology. He completed his doctorate at Leiden University in 2015 under Peter Bisschop, having also studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane, and held posts at University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Leiden University.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from Cambridge. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India from 1929, ultimately serving as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950) and later advisor (~1950–1952).

Nirbhay N. Singh is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).

Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University. He served at the National Archives of India (~1942–1953) and was founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987).
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2003, later serving as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied and earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1964–1994) and served as a professor at Taisho University (~1994–2008).
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, and others, later serving as professor at Otani University (~1980–2015).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara. He held assistant professor posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota is a scholar of Indology and history who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He held a research fellowship at the University of Tokyo (~1998–2001) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He was a research student at Taisho University and held a post as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from around 1951 to 1959 and served there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).

Tensho Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2011). He held posts at Toyo University (~2011–2014), the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and Tokyo University of Agriculture (attested 2015).
